sections.skill: Pick which details in a plan need checking

questions.prompt: In the example, which detail goes in the CHECK pile?

choices.text: The idea of having a picnic

questions.intro: Sort each detail in a plan into one of two piles. CHECK pile: anything that could cost money, time or safety if wrong, such as prices, hours, schedules, entry rules, bookings, weather, allergies and local laws. LOW-RISK pile: ideas and preferences, such as "visit a bookstore" or "have pasta on Tuesday," where being wrong costs little. Example plan: "Saturday: zoo opens 9 a.m., tickets 15 dollars; then a picnic." Check pile: zoo hours, ticket price. Low-risk: the picnic idea.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Make plans robust and confirm bookings

questions.prompt: A plan includes a popular museum that requires advance tickets. What could go wrong?

choices.text: The museum will be too empty
Nothing, since museums always sell tickets at the door
Arriving without tickets and being turned away

questions.correct_answer: Arriving without tickets and being turned away
questions.intro: Plans can fail in small ways that add up: a museum that requires advance tickets, a hike that takes longer than estimated, a recipe that assumes an ingredient is easy to find. Safety details deserve special care: food allergies, medication timing, weather warnings, and trail conditions should come from reliable sources, not a general plan. Building in slack time and a backup option makes a plan more robust. When a plan involves bookings or payments, confirm directly with the provider.
